agent_flags.outcome_note: Accepted, attempted 2026-09-08, REVERTED. `pnpm add -D pa11y-ci` pulled in puppeteer@24.43.1, whose build script pnpm declines to run; pnpm's dep-status check then failed `pnpm install` with exit 1, which broke EVERY pnpm-run command including `pnpm dev`, `tsc`, `eslint` and `pnpm build`. Declaring pnpm.ignoredBuiltDependencies in apps/web/package.json did not clear it; the correct location is `allowBuilds` in apps/web/pnpm-workspace.yaml, which already carries an `unrs-resolver: true` entry and a comment weighing exactly this allow-vs-deny trade-off. The install also left a literal placeholder line (`puppeteer: set this to true or false`) in that file, which was caught and reverted while computing the round-2 gate snapshot -- it would otherwise have reached the commit. So the mechanism is known and small; what remains out of scope is the ~150MB browser download decision and the absence of anything to scan. Install reverted; toolchain verified restored (tsc/eslint clean, 99 vitest, build OK, package.json + lockfile byte-clean). Two further findings that change the calculus: (1) approving the build downloads ~150MB of Chromium, a stack decision belonging in an ADR -- ADR-0001 never chose a browser runner; (2) there is currently NOTHING meaningful to scan -- every apps/web route redirects to Keycloak or /login without a session, and the only page rendering HTML unauthenticated is Next's built-in 404. Wiring design_check today would convert an honest N/A into a misleading PASS over a framework error page, which the evidence-pass anti-suppression rules exist to prevent. Needs its own change: browser-provisioning decision + ADR + project-commands/stack-smoke config-drift updates + an authenticated scan path. Verdict left as `accept` -- verdicts are not editable -- with this outcome recorded instead.
